chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a man who married a young girl, had intercourse with her, and consummated the marriage. He said: Upon him is the obligation to maintain her (provide for her upkeep) as long as she is alive. This does not contradict the first report, because we interpret this report as referring to one who had intercourse with her after nine years. For there is no diyah (blood money) upon him, but rather the obligation of maintenance upon him as long as she is alive, because she is not suitable for a man. And this interpretation does not contradict his statement in the first report: 'If he wishes, he divorces her; and if he wishes, he keeps her,' when the intercourse is after nine years, because the choice has been established for him between keeping her and divorcing her, and neither of them is obligatory upon him. And although maintenance upon her is obligatory upon him in all cases, as we have presented. And as for the report which...

key_terms.أَفْضَاهَا: he consummated the marriage / had intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: What is the financial and marital obligation for a man who consummates marriage with a young girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between two hadiths by distinguishing the age of consummation: if the girl is under nine years old, the husband bears no diyah liability but must maintain her indefinitely as she remains valid for marriage, whereas consummation after age nine triggers different legal implications. This interpretation highlights the Shia juristic principle of reconciling conflicting narrations through contextual differentiation (tarjih) rather than abrogation. The ruling underscores the enduring obligation of nafaqah regardless of the husband's choice to retain or divorce the wife.
